title: WeMacro Bluetooth FOCUSER_STEPS stays BUSY after a disconnect during a move
description: In indigo_mac_drivers/focuser_wemacro_bt/indigo_focuser_wemacro_bt.m the didDisconnectPeripheral callback (reached on Bluetooth link loss and on a CONNECTION disconnect) does not end a FOCUSER_STEPS move that is in INDIGO_BUSY_STATE. FOCUSER_STEPS is completed only by a 0xf5/0xf6 notification from the rail, which can no longer arrive, so the property stays BUSY across the disconnect and reconnect. The FOCUSER_STEPS change handler starts a move only when the state is not BUSY, so every later move request is silently ignored until FOCUSER_ABORT_MOTION sets ALERT. Expected: a disconnect while FOCUSER_STEPS is BUSY ends the move with INDIGO_ALERT_STATE (as was done for X_RAIL_EXECUTE in ticket a2513f61-8af8-4ff2-a950-7bf0658d19a0 and as the portable sibling indigo_drivers/focuser_wemacro does), and a move requested after reconnect is accepted. Add hardware-free regression coverage in indigo_test/unit/test_focuser_wemacro_bt.py and increment DRIVER_VERSION. Found by the reviewer of ticket a2513f61 as a pre-existing, out-of-scope issue; not measured on the physical rail.

outcome.summary: Not a defect: indigo_focuser_change_property already resets FOCUSER_STEPS to OK and deletes it on disconnect, so it does not stay BUSY across a reconnect. Owner decided to discard the implemented ALERT notification.

history.text: Implementer launched; reading driver and test

Reproduced: new FOCUSER_STEPS assertions in test_focuser_wemacro_bt.py fail on the unmodified didDisconnectPeripheral (state stays BUSY, no update). After fix: test passes (3 tests OK). Fix publishes ALERT update before the base indigo_focuser_change_property call; note the base class itself resets FOCUSER_STEPS to OK on disconnect (indigo_focuser_driver.c:184) after that. Not measured on the physical rail.

The ticket's premise is wrong: indigo_focuser_change_property (indigo_libs/indigo_focuser_driver.c:184), called at the end of didDisconnectPeripheral, already sets FOCUSER_STEPS to OK and deletes it on disconnect, so it does not stay BUSY across a reconnect. The implemented change only publishes ALERT for a BUSY FOCUSER_STEPS just before the property is deleted (plus a test and DRIVER_VERSION 0x02000007). Owner decision: close the ticket unresolved as not a defect and discard the change, or keep the change as a client-visible ALERT notification and continue to review?
Owner: close the ticket as unresolved (not a defect) and discard the change.
